No message in the delta contains plural, select, selectordinal or pound, so no CLDR category set applies to these 38 and none is missing; es plurals elsewhere (one/many/other, never few) were not exercised by this delta.

Rendered every value with intl-messageformat 12.1.3 under locale 'es' and read the output as a native reader: all 38 compose readable Spanish. Then rendered the argument-bearing keys against ten adversarial names (vowel-initial, article-initial, embedded typographic quotes, embedded comma, very long, CJK, RTL, Latin/RTL mixed, digit-initial, apostrophe) and three labels: no elision, agreement, case, classifier or word-order break; the quotes stay outside every name; nested-quote and RTL-inside-LTR cases behave exactly as the English does.

Composition checked at the call sites: the sidebar pin control's aria-label stays 'Fijar “{name}”' while its tooltip toggles to 'Desfijar “{name}”' with aria-pressed carrying the state (chat-sidebar.tsx:7130-7150); the header chip's accessible name is the whole sentence the sidecar describes (chat-header-identity.tsx:470-490); the rename control uses rename/cancel/saving as aria-label + title on a 20px icon button (chat-header.tsx:905-930), so no button width is at stake; chatRegionLabel() feeds the F6 region walk (chat-regions.ts:82-92); the action rows pick their label by kind (message-actions-row.tsx:528-536); checkpointAriaLabel() passes {clock} only when checkpointClockLabel() returns a non-empty string (checkpoint-model.ts:237-259), so the no-clock form is used instead of an empty time.

Typography and encoding: all 38 are NFC; no leading/trailing space, no double space, no straight quotes or apostrophe, ellipsis is U+2026, quotes are U+201C/U+201D, no space before : ; ? !, no '!', no NBSP/NNBSP, no bidi or zero-width control characters, no BOM. JSON parses in every file; no key added or dropped against English (parity test above).

Width: none of the 38 carries a maxCells hint in its sidecar, so fit was judged against the English and the chrome each string lands in: visible strings are the row-menu items (18-24 cells vs 16-22 English), the two tooltips (14-18 and 15-25 cells) and the rail lead line ('Turno 3 de 7' 12 vs 'Turn 3 of 7' 11); the remaining 30 are accessible names or screen-reader-only group labels with no width budget. No overflow risk found.

Second pass on the high-visibility groups (ui.chat, ui.chat.header): re-read with a different lens (each string as the state it names and the control it names it on, rather than string-by-string), plus a re-check of every finding decision. Nothing was added and nothing withdrawn.
